title: Sharing and Reusing Code
text: These questions check that you can share code between modules and workbooks, load libraries safely, and decide how far to trust code from elsewhere.

tasks.text: A JADE code module is named Report Tools and contains function summarize(rows). How do you call it from another module?
A classmate sends you a gist ID for a JADE module you haven't read. Which is the safer first step?
choices: Add await Jade.load_gist(id) to your auto_exec
Import it with Jade.import_code_module, then read it before running anything
Run it on your real workbook to see what it does
Paste the ID into your platform profile

tasks.text: Which library address is pinned to a version?
An assistant writes a loader named autoExec, and it never runs. Why did the assistant use that name, and what should you add to your platform profile?
tasks.answer: Its style rule said to use camelCase, and it applied that to a name JADE requires (auto_exec), so JADE never found it. Add a line saying JADE's required names, like auto_exec, win over the camelCase rule.

tasks.text: Explain what happens every time a workbook with await Jade.load_gist("...", "harvest_app") in its auto_exec is opened, and what that means for trust.
tasks.answer: JADE checks the gist and runs its current code (downloading again only if it changed), with full access to the workbook. Whoever controls the gist controls what runs; changes reach every workbook automatically. Use it for code whose author you trust; never put secrets in a gist.

tasks.text: Write a function kilogramsByBed(harvestRows) that returns an object of total kilograms by bed ID, from rows where row 0 is the header, B (index 1) is Bed ID and D (index 3) is Kilograms. Then write testKilogramsByBed, which logs JSON.stringify(kilogramsByBed(rows)) for rows = [["Date", "Bed ID", "Crop", "Kilograms"], ["2027-04-18", "B2", "Radish", 1.2], ["2027-05-13", "B4", "Spinach", 2.4], ["2027-05-15", "B2", "Lettuce", 3.9]].

Start a new chat with your learner profile and your updated JADE platform profile. Ask for a JADE panel with a pie chart of total kilograms by crop, using Chart.js. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Did it follow the new rule: where the library comes from, with a pinned version? (3) Check the chart's labels and numbers against the Harvests sheet for two crops. (4) If anything conflicted with your profiles or with JADE's documentation, write a new platform profile line for it.
tasks.answer: Full credit: notes source and pinning; checks two crops (e.g. Bean 10.1, Tomato 10.2); any new conflict turned into a profile line. Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
